To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have discovered and studied the light echo of the supernova SN 2003gd.

a light echo has been discovered around SN 2003gd, the echo is due to dust grains in front of the supernova, the grains appear to be more silicate‐rich than Galactic grains, and the echo is more consistent with a distance of 7 Mpc.

the light echo around SN 2003gd can be explained by a sheet of grains with Galactic composition located ∼113 parsecs from the supernova, and the echo is more consistent with a distance to the SN host galaxy of 7 Mpc rather than 9 Mpc, as suggested by the literature.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the physics of light scattering by small particles, and with its applications to astrophysics, in particular to the study of the structure and composition of interstellar dust and the interstellar medium in general.
the study of the interstellar medium, and in particular with the study of interstellar dust.
the development of a new method for the analysis of the structure and dynamics of complex systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

SN 2003gd is a Type II‐plateausupernova with a progenitor mass between 8 and 12 M _{☉} and a distance of 7.5 ± 1.5 Mpc, which exploded ∼113 pc behind a dust sheet with a column density of 1.3 × 10 ^{20} cm ^{-2}.
the dust in the light echo around SN 2003gd appears to be more similar to Galactic dust than to the carbon‐rich dust in the Small Magellanic Cloud.
the light echo is consistent with a SN explosion in a relatively low mass progenitor, and that the progenitor was not a Wolf‐Rayet star.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the SN light pulse is scattered by a dust cloud located ∼113 parsec in front of SN 2003gd, and that these dust grains are very similar to those assumed to be present in the interstellar medium in our own Galaxy.

the light echo is consistent with a SN progenitor of initial mass M _{i} ∼8 M _{sun} and a distance D ∼ 7 Mpc, but that it is also consistent with M _{i} ≳ 12 M _{sun} at D ≲ 9 Mpc, with the most probable progenitor mass being in the range 10...
the echo is a valuable probe of the properties of dust grains, but that it is not an unambiguous indicator of the distance to the SN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the light echo around SN 2003gd can be explained by the scattering of SN light off grains that are not unlike those in the diffuse interstellar medium of the Galaxy.
the echo can be used to probe the properties of the circumstellar medium and the interstellar medium along the line of sight.
the echo around SN 2003gd is not a unique phenomenon.
